In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the dipa ligand to dimerise or polymerise transition metal complexes.
the role of dipaH(4) in cluster dinitrogen chemistry and cluster dimerisation/polymerisation.
the synthesis of novel metal complexes, the structural elucidation of these compounds and the study of their magnetic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dipaH3 ligand is able to induce cluster dimerisation or polymerisation and the nature of the magnetic behaviour is dependent on both the nature of the metal centre and the bridging ligand.
the spin ground state is S= 1, with a small component of the excited state, S= 3, which is consistent with the experimental data.

the presence of dipaH(4) in 1 and the presence of dipamH(3) in 3 induce the dimerisation/polymerisation of two different starting complexes and the resulting clusters show no evidence of single molecule magnet behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

dipaH(+) is not a simple spectator ligand in the synthesis of the Fe(6) complexes but rather a key component of the dimerisation process and that the flexibility of this ligand is also a key feature in the formation of the polymer in 3.
the presence of the flexible dipaH(4) ligand in these clusters is responsible for the formation of the dimerised and polymerised structures.

the flexible dipaH(4) ligand has been used to synthesise two hexanuclear S= 5 spin frustrated Fe(6) cluster complexes and a new one-dimensional covalent polymer with a novel mixed valence [3Co(II)-Co(III)] cluster motif.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of dipaH(4) ligands is not only responsible for the formation of hexanuclear Fe clusters of S= 6 and 7, but also of the 1D polymer 3.
the flexible amino-alcohols, dipaH(4) and dipamH(4), can be used to control the dimerisation and/or polymerisation of transition metal clusters and complexes.
the flexible amino-alcohols are able to induce the formation of both the hexanuclear spin frustrated S= Fe6 clusters and the 1D covalently bonded mixed valence [CobIIICoIII] polymer.
